$comment: The canonical source of the version a native publish may carry. `release/publish-packages.json`
does this job for the npm packages; nothing did it for the three native ones, whose version came
from a `workflow_dispatch` text box and was checked only for semver *shape*. A Maven Central
coordinate is immutable, a pub.dev version is permanent and a SwiftPM tag is what `from:`
resolves against forever, so the number is the one release decision that cannot be corrected —
and it was the one release decision no reviewed file recorded.
A real publish now reads this file. `node scripts/check-native-publish-preflight.mjs
--authorize-version=<v> --line=<key>` runs in each publish workflow in a step carrying
`if: ${{ inputs.dry_run == false }}`, so the dispatch input is a *confirmation* of what is
declared here rather than the source of it, and a version reaches a registry only after it has
been through review.
THE FIXTURE SEAM IS PROHIBITED IN A PUBLISH WORKFLOW. `--lines-file=` exists only so ci.yml can
prove the authorization accepts one version and refuses five others against the fixtures in
scripts/publish/fixtures/native-release-lines/. VI-VERSION-AUTHORIZED rejects it in any publish
workflow, because a test seam reachable from the publish path is a bypass — and this one was:
aimed at the accepting fixture, a publish step authorized 0.1.0 while this file authorized
nothing, and every other structural check still passed. A run that uses the override labels its
own output as a fixture run, so such a log cannot later read as a real authorization.
A DRY RUN IS DELIBERATELY NOT GATED ON THIS FILE. Rehearsing the release path with an arbitrary
shape-valid version is how a defect in that path is found without publishing, so the
authorization step is gated by the same step-level condition as the publication itself and
nothing else in either workflow depends on this file.
FIELDS
coordinate       what the registry would show. Pinned against the manifests by the
ID-* checks in the preflight; repeated here so this file can be read alone.
channel          the registry.
cohort           which release line this package follows. `own` = its own version line,
independent of the npm packages. `core` = lockstep with the @kinetixui/{tokens,ui,cli}
cohort. DECLARED, never inferred from a number: npm `0.27.0` and a native
`0.27.0` would be the same string and two unrelated promises.
published        every version this line has actually published, oldest first. A version in
this list can never be authorized again; on Central and pub.dev the attempt
fails anyway, and for SwiftUI it would move a tag consumers already resolve.
authorizedNext   the single version the next real publish may carry, or null.
COHORT IS DECIDED: `own` ON ALL THREE LINES. Owner decision, 2026-11-09. The native libraries
declare no dependency on the npm core cohort — they consume generated token output rather than
depending on @kinetixui/tokens — and their registries' release mechanics differ, so lockstep
with npm would assert a coupling nothing enforces. Each native line versions independently.
NULL `authorizedNext` MEANS NO PUBLISH IS AUTHORIZED, AND THAT IS THE CURRENT STATE. No native
package has ever been published, and the registry prerequisites for all three lines are
outstanding, so `authorizedNext` is null on every line and every real native publish fails
closed at the authorization step. There is no fallback and no inference: a publish becomes
possible when somebody commits a number here, which is the point.
THE APPROVED FIRST PUBLIC VERSION OF EACH LINE IS 0.1.0 (owner decision, 2026-11-09). That is a
release PLAN, recorded here and in RELEASING.md, and it is deliberately NOT written into
`authorizedNext`: planning a number and authorizing its publication are different decisions, and
only the second one opens the door. A later dedicated release-authorization pull request sets
`authorizedNext` per line, and only once that line's registry prerequisites are verified —
for Flutter that includes the pub.dev verified publisher for kinetixui.com actually existing,
its domain verification succeeding, the intended Google account owning it, and kinetix_ui being
associated with it. None of those facts is established today and none may be assumed.
Setting `authorizedNext` is a release decision, not a formality. Changing it is a reviewable
diff in a pull request; after a publish, move the number into `published` and set
`authorizedNext` back to null in the same commit that records the release.
